title: Pay-Per-Click (PPC) Advertising
description: This is a competency-based course designed for the indentured Digital Marketer apprentice. Apprentices will gain hands-on experience in setting up and managing PPC campaigns using Google Ads and social media platforms. The course also covers budgeting, targeting strategies, and conversion tracking.
learning_objectives: Explain how a paid search auction decides which ad shows and what it costs
Structure a paid account into campaigns and ad groups that can be optimized
Select keywords and match types, and use negatives to protect budget
Write compliant ad copy and assets that match the query and the landing page
Set budgets, bidding strategies, and targeting for a stated campaign goal
Plan a paid social campaign and choose the audiences for it
Implement conversion tracking and verify that it reports correctly
Improve the conversion rate of a landing page receiving paid traffic
Design a valid A/B test on ads or landing pages and interpret the result
Judge campaign performance on return on investment and decide what to change
prerequisites: dm201 Search Engine Optimization (SEO), for keyword research and search intent

sequencing_rationale: Paid media punishes structural mistakes with real money, so the course front-loads mechanism and structure (02-03) before anything is launched, then works outward through the levers a campaign actually exposes: keywords (04), creative and policy (05), money and targeting (06), then the second platform family, paid social (07). Measurement infrastructure (08) precedes optimization (09-11) because optimizing on untrusted conversion data is the most common failure in this discipline; the capstone is small because the preceding lessons are already hands-on. SCOPE ASSUMPTIONS - this intake description is one of the two in the pathway that is NOT truncated, so scope is better evidenced here than elsewhere, but it still supplied no objectives or lesson titles: (1) 'Google Ads and social media platforms' is taken at face value - Google Ads is the primary teaching platform (it is named in the intake) and lesson 07 covers paid social generically with Meta and LinkedIn as the worked examples; the reviewer should confirm which ad accounts apprentices can access. (2) 'Budgeting, targeting strategies, and conversion tracking' are the three named requirements and get dedicated coverage (lessons 06 and 08). (3) A/B testing and landing-page CRO are included because the catalog sites D3-S1-C02 in the PPC domain; deeper CRO and UX work is dm301's. (4) Programmatic/display networks, YouTube video ads, retail media and app-install campaigns are OUT of scope at 60 hours - flag if any is expected. (5) Learners are assumed to work in sandbox or draft campaigns; no lesson requires live ad spend.

proposed_competencies.competency_text: The learner can forecast paid media spend and pace a budget across a flight against a target cost per acquisition.
proposed_competencies.rationale: Lesson 06 and the capstone both require forecasting and pacing spend, which is what an employer checks first; D3-S1-C01 mentions bids and D3-S1-C03 covers reading ROI after the fact, but neither covers planning spend forward.
